text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @oncall-inference — Sev 2 / multicell collective failures detected in dedicated-gpu-prod-us-west2. Symptoms: repeated NCCL hangs during allreduce, intermittent container restarts on worker nodes, and a flurry of CUDA errors. Affected model pool: redwood/llama-13b-quant (tensor/pipeline parallel groups).

pagerduty: Acknowledged by sasha (oncall). ETA 5m.

sasha: I'm on it, looking at the node list and recent kube events. Can someone grab the node-level dmesg?

mike: grabbing logs now. initial pattern: `ncclCommInitRank failed: Unhandled system error` followed by containers stuck in `S` and kernel messages showing `GPU hung` and `kernel driver reloaded`. Also seeing `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in one stack trace.

carol: Customer impact: CS reports 3 production customers with streaming 502s and increased tail latency for embeddings. Telemetry: 95th latency spikes to ~12s, throughput down ~30% for that pool.

anna: quick mitigation thought: isolate offending pods and failover traffic to fallback pool (single-gpu variant). We can also set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 to drop IB usage if IB path is flapping.

sasha: taking action: cordon + drain node gpu-node-17, evicting pods. Running: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

mike: watching pod restarts. Also running `nvidia-smi -q` on gpu-node-17 — GPUs show processes stuck with high GPU utilization but no cpu time. PID 28431 in container `inference-worker` is spinning in kernel.

dave: I see repeated NCCL timeouts in the worker logs: 
```
[I] 2026-03-15T21:02:12Z nccl INFO AllReduce: timeout 120s
[E] 2026-03-15T21:02:14Z nccl ERROR ncclCommDestroy error - "unhandled system error"
```
Looks like the communicator becomes corrupt and later triggers CUDA faults.

infra-bot: Node gpu-node-17 reported kernel oops and automatic reboot at 21:05:40 UTC. Marked NotReady by kubelet.

sasha: gpu-node-17 is flapping — cordoned and removed. Shifting traffic via rollout to dedicated-gpu-prod-us-west1. Triggering canary route for 5% -> 25%.

mike: trying NCCL debug envs on a repro node: `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL` — dumping communicator state. Also trying `NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=SYS` to force system-level p2p.

carol: Noting customer-facing update sent by CS: "We're investigating a latency/regression affecting gen/embeddings in US-West; temporary degraded routing may occur. We'll update in 30m."

anna: quick hotfix applied to deployment template for fallback pool: set `env: [ { name: "NCCL_IB_DISABLE", value: "1" }, { name: "NCCL_P2P_LEVEL", value: "SYS" } ]` and restarted canary pods.

mike: after restart, canary pods booted and began serving. Observed fewer allreduce hangs. Still seeing 1-2 residual illegal memory accesses in older pods.

sasha: handoff: @mike taking lead for the next 30m while I coordinate with infra to check kernel/driver mismatch. Leaving a note: suspected recent driver roll (nvidia-driver-525 -> 535) on a subset of nodes; mismatch across nodes can break NCCL collectives.

mike: confirmed: gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-19 are on driver 535, gpu-node-17 was on 525. That's likely the root cause — communicator formation expects same driver/driver ABI across ranks.

customer-success-bot: CS updated affected customers with "We're routing traffic to unaffected capacity and investigating; some requests may be retried automatically."

anna: mitigation checklist completed:
- cordon + drain flapping nodes
- roll canary to stable pool with env overrides
- apply temporary traffic split (25% west1, 75% west2-stable)
- notify CS + customers

mike: running cluster-wide audit: `kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,DRIVER:.status.nodeInfo.kernelVersion` and also cross-check nvidia-driver via `ssh node -- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv`. Preparing a small automation to patch driver mismatch.

sasha: infra confirmed they will standardize driver to 535 across affected zone. They are scheduling rolling reboots with cordon/drain. ETA for full rollout 2h.

dave: added a temporary safeguard in the runtime: if NCCL communicator init fails for a group, fallback to `model-variant: single-gpu` for that request and emit a metric `nccl_comm_fallback=1`. Patching config and pushing to canary.

mike: monitoring after changes: error rate returning to baseline for canary, latency trending down. No new container restarts in last 8m.

sasha: oncall note for incident record — probable cause: driver version skew across nodes causing NCCL communicator formation failures and subsequent CUDA faults leading to container restarts and node flaps. Immediate mitigations: node isolation, traffic failover, env overrides (NCCL_IB_DISABLE/NCCL_P2P_LEVEL), runtime fallback to single-gpu.

carol: tally customer impact: 3 customers degraded for ~22m, no data loss, automatic retries mitigated some requests. CS to follow up with post-incident notes.

infra-bot: Rolling upgrade to nvidia-driver-535 started at 21:28 UTC (gpu-node-10 first). Progress: 2/8 nodes updated.

mike: leaving final checks enabled for next hour — will escalate back to oncall if error rate increases.

sasha: thanks team, I'm closing active page. Please add any logs to this thread. Postmortem owners: sasha + infra.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged as mitigated. Pager cleared.

carol: adding a quick runbook action item: add driver-version check to pre-deploy validation for gpu pools and a monitoring alert when driver version skew > 0 across nodes.

anna: noted. I'll create a small gating CI to check `nvidia-smi` versions before rolling a model deployment.

mike: saved core logs and NCCL debug dump to s3://redwood-incidents/1865571234/nccl-dump.tar.gz.

sasha: final: ticket created INC-2026-1849, linking to this thread and assigning postmortem.

carol: :thumbsup: closing out.
